steps.text: 2:18 P.M. \ Clear
Deserted Coastal Town, North of Iberia
We've arrived at the specified coordinates.
The target building's outside appearance matches the description outlined in the preliminary survey report.
Our team will now proceed into the building for an inspection. We may need to cut the transmission. Watch for flares, in case anything happens.
Blue Poison, over and out.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: There's an entrance here. Hm, it doesn't look like the builders intended for this to be here.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: The edges are pretty rough, like it was hacked open with an axe. Perhaps the bounty hunters did this? I heard some of them like to come 'treasure hunting' here.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: That's probably because they aren't Iberians...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Right, ruins like this one are more than 'toxic' to those who got out of that alive.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: As for the ones that stayed behind... The Church, the Inquisition... They have no way to make it here.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: They already pay too high a price, and they wouldn't want to see any of this.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's just like how I never wanted to look at my legs when I was a kid. No matter how much I tried, they just couldn't run. Iberia as it is now doesn't want to see any of these broken parts.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Look at you, using yourself as an analogy again. I'm starting to feel bad.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm, I can tell you are joking this time.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Electromagnetic Pulse Field released.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: So, should we go up? Or down?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Your call.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I'm thinking up. I'm not entirely sure why, but I feel up is the way to go. This place is like... a tower.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: A tower? How tall do you think it is? The part that stands above ground is at most three stories. What could its purpose be?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: In that case, I guess we should go down.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You just reminded me that we have no idea how far down it might go.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Let's find out, then. And don't worry. I got your back.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: That puts my mind at ease, though I do hope we won't end up in a fight.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Hm, it's dark in here.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: The lighting system is busted.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You can't fix it?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: The Iberian technology here is several decades old. Their wiring is nothing like Raythean's. If you gave me a few days...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Don't worry about it, then. We'll let Closure and Engineering worry about it later. We won't be staying in this coffin pit for long.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Coffin?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It's an analogy, or maybe not. There is a foul stench lingering in this building.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's been abandoned for years, and then it was flooded with seawater and buried by mud...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Shh.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Say, if we don't talk, do you suppose we'll hear ghosts screaming?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: G-Ghosts...?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Oh, it's just a joke. Try not to tug so hard on my clothes. I like this new outfit a lot.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh... We should switch on our portable Originium lamps.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Now it's much brighter.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You seem to be a big fan of these technological ruins.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: This kind of technology only existed in the coastal towns of the past. You don't see them much in Iberia these days.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: What... are they for?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: For observation? To relay signals? Or could it be... for sightseeing?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Perhaps it was for locking people up.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Possibly...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: When we look at the Iberia of the past, we some see the technology that they left behind, like gold covered in dust.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Yet, during those radiant times, there were countless bones buried underneath El Dorado.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: What are you apologizing for? The bones of the Ægirs who took my ancestors away to Iberia have long been eroded by the sea waves.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I don't hate Iberia, nor do I hate the Ægir people. Now, I suppose I don't even hate myself as much anymore. This is all thanks to the Doctor and you, Glau.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Does this technology... give you any bad memories?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: All I care about is whether this place will be of any use to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: In the end, this is what we are here for, no?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Right... We're here to scout out the surroundings, to analyze the data, and to confirm what we can retrieve.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Too bad that this place has been torn apart inside and out, though. If it was just the time and the environment, the parts wouldn't be this wrecked.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Look at this part here. It went so far... Ah!

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: What's wrong? Why did you pull out your Franker all of a sudden...?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: T-There's a ghost!

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: A ghost...? You mean the shadow in the path ahead?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It isn't moving. Doesn't seem to be alive.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Judging from his getup... It seems he was a bounty hunter.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: We haven't made it very far from the entrance. Perhaps he was the one who cracked it open, and he died here after he came inside.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, I see.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Wait, let's not get any closer yet.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: We still don't know how he died.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: You think it could be dangerous?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: A bounty hunter died so close to the entrance.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: We'll have to watch out for whatever killed him.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Stand back a little more.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I can smell... the scent of the seawater.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Seawater? We're pretty far away from the shore.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You don't mean...
Though Blue Poison told Glaucus to stay where she is, she continues to walk toward the corpse. She kneels down about a meter away, observing it closely.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Okay, it's just some seagrass.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It's a full skeleton. No sign that he was eaten by any monsters, and there are no other fatal injuries.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: *Sniffs*

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: No trace of any common toxins that could lead to death either.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Judging from his posture, he likely got himself tied up in the seagrass and drowned.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I don't see any water, though. It's dry everywhere.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Take a closer look at the rust left on the wall.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm... I can see some areas are more rusted than others.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: So this place was flooded twice, then?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: The seawater destroyed the building the first time around. Whatever its function was, that was when it failed. The second time, the seawater gushed into this place again, flooding its insides once more.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: And this poor bastard happened to be in here at the time. He likely thought he'd hit the jackpot, and was happily tearing away at the things in the wall.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: He didn't manage to escape in time when the seawater began to flood the building, and the seagrass had his arms and legs caught. He lost his life after struggling for a while.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You can't really blame him. He was a Kuranta.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Poor guy... They don't know the strength of the sea.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: The Doctor once mentioned that research on the ocean is for the most part done only by a handful of oceanologists. It's not a very popular field.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Well, it's not really that strange. We are only interested in the things that we can see and conquer.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Perhaps... the Iberia of the past was the sole exception.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's all in the past. I haven't seen the ocean myself either.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm... I'm not even sure why you're so sensitive to the scent of seawater.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Have you heard that rumor?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: About the disasters?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: We... don't talk about that. That's not allowed in Iberia.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You're all used to avoiding the subject.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's hard to kick your habits. We don't talk much about... our homeland at Rhodes Island. Besides, each of us has a different impression of that incident, and sometimes even about that whole area.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I've talked to Weedy about it. Both of us are Ægirs who grew up in Iberia, and I've come to realize the Iberia in her eyes is totally different from the one I see.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: That's nothing strange, no? If you are not allowed to discuss the incident, then the only thing you will remember of it is the small fragment that you saw with your own eyes.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: They... are taking the chance to piece the fragments together, from the people.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm, there's only the two of us now. I could talk about it, but... I'm afraid to do that. It's like something has my throat blocked.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I'm worried that as soon as I talk, the shadows cast on the path here will charge toward me.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: And I say that even though I know it's just shadows cast by the Originium lamp.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Shadows... What a fine analogy. They skillfully redirect everyone's attention away, such that they fear the shadows rather than the enormous truth that lies behind.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's so cold... but I'm sweating.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: In the past, I would never even imagine that I could stand here and talk to you about this.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Everyone feels that way.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I suppose this pitch-black, sealed-off building is protecting us.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: There's a dead body here, and we don't know what lies ahead. But this keeps me even more at ease than a wide open space.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: The walls here give us a false sense of security, a sense that everything's under our control.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: You're right. At least there isn't another pair of eyes staring at us.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Now I'm not sure about that.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Stop trying to scare me...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Okay, okay. I'll stop. Back to the topic of the disaster. The Inquisition isn't actually to blame for that decision. The decision to not talk about that was made by the Ægirs who came ashore.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I guess it was a form of self protection.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Self... protection?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Do you know why the Ægirs came ashore?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I... don't know. I thought we were meant to be here to begin with, though it seems most Iberians don't agree with that.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I'm not too familiar either.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Yeah... but you know more than we do, at the very least.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It's funny. The history slowly disappeared from the Ægirs' memories, and we are the ones who still remember any of it.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: My ancestors were taken away by the Ægirs some hundred years ago. They wanted the 'toxic' ability that we are born with.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Why... is that?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: They kept extracting the toxins for experiments. They were trying to figure out whether these subterranean toxins could be used as some kind of weapon...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: What were they trying to attack with that?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I have no idea. How could I have seen it? From my elders tell me, it was an enormous, terrifying monster that doesn't exist on land.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: It's from the sea...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: All I can say is that's extraordinarily likely.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I thought about asking the Doctor or Dr. Kal'tsit... or even the hunters directly.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Once, I happened upon Operator Skadi. This question immediately rose to the top of my mind.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I doubt she'd tell you...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Right, I don't think so either, and I didn't ask her in the end.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I'm not sure I have the courage to find out the truth...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Just like the Ægirs who came ashore, it took them several hundred years to forget that fear. That's how they could finally put down roots with their minds at ease to slowly become a part of Iberia.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: No one would cast aside a new life they earned for themselves to fight what could be an endless war. Especially not when nobody knows when that disaster would actually strike, and when it actually strikes, everything could still be futile.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Even I wish that I could live a new life, even after the Doctor has taught me so much.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: In that case... perhaps we should turn back, then?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: We can still make it.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: You're still going straight ahead...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Oh, you're right. I'm still going straight.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Thinking back, after all these years, I haven't once thought of giving up my abilities to use my toxin.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Perhaps I've never managed to break free of the souls of those Ægirs who enslaved my ancestors, and, deep down in my heart, I believe that the toxins in me will get the enemies they're meant for.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: How far down have we come?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I lost track.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Me too.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: This tower is deeper than I expected... Uh, taller. The confined space here is disrupting our senses.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh, I think I'm hallucinating.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: What did you see?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Blinks)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: A light up ahead.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: And it's slowly floating upwards.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (Quietly) Switch your light off!
Amid the darkness, there is a white light swaying not far away.
Blue Poison makes sure this isn't a reflection of their lamps. Is it an illusion, or is it real? Which scenario is more dangerous?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (Let's get closer. Slowly now, don't surprise them.)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Is it a threat?)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (Prepare for combat...)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Franker at the ready.)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (Okay, we'll be making contact soon. There's a corner up ahead. Watch my hand. I'll knock three times. On the count of three—)
A bolt whizzes through the air.
It strikes the fuzzy white light. No, not quite. Just as it was about to strike the object, its trajectory curved to the side.
It's no problem. No one can see it. The bolt split in two soon after it was shot, one in the front, and one in the back, capturing the white light.
The very next moment, the white light suddenly expands.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Franker, maximum power!
W-Wait!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Amplifying microwave—
I mean no harm!

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Hm?
*Cough*... Oww... hit my back... what a shockwave...
Please don't do that again...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: If it's mercy you want, you should stop casting, Caster.
Uh, you mean my light? N-No, you're mistaken. This is just for lighting up my surroundings.
I defended myself on reflex. Please believe me! I don't want to hurt you at all!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: No wonder... it feels kind of warm... and bright... Nothing about it makes me feel sick.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Glau, don't let your guard down just yet.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Her Originium Arts are not to be underestimated. This seems a little special, even.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Hm...
P-Put it down, please! Could you also move your bolt away from my neck...? Just a little, please?
I... I'm too scared to even breathe now... *Whimpers*...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I can lower my crossbow.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: But you need to drop your staff too. If you try anything funny, believe me, your reflexes are no match for my bolts.
Okay...
The light extinguishes as soon as the girl throws her staff away.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Originium lamp.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Alright.
So that light was yours...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Are you after us?
No, that isn't what I meant.
I was waiting down below. There's no one else here, and when I saw your light, I thought maybe somebody decided to check this place out, so I started climbing the stairs to meet this guest.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You said you've been here for a while. Who are you?
Oh, I forgot to introduce myself... Um, my name is Aria.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Well, Aria, are you an Iberian?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Yes. Why, is it obvious?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I figured I'd ask. If you'd said no, I would've guessed Columbian or Victorian. I have my ways to make you talk.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Why, that's sending chills down my spine...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You're an Iberian and a Caster, and your Originium Arts work as a light. Are you affiliated with the Inquisition?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: The Inquisition? No, no, no! I haven't ever met them.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: What are you doing here, then?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Isn't this almost an interrogation? We're just here to check this place out.)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (It's more efficient to ask her directly. Besides, it doesn't seem like she noticed anything's off yet.)

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Mmm... What am I doing here again?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Why, I'm not actually so sure myself...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Hm? Do you have amnesia, perhaps?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: No, of course not. I remember how I got here and that I spent the last couple days here.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Two days ago, I asked a local about any opportunities to make some money in the area. I needed work... Otherwise I would go hungry.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: He took the last few coins I had and told me I could come seek riches here.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Sounds like she ran into a con man...)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: He might've mistaken you for a bounty hunter.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: A lot of bounty hunters used to come to this area in the past. You have a staff, and you, well... you look like you are from a rather well off family, by your appearance. They may have thought you an aristocratic young lady looking for adventure.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Oh... Is that it? So they misunderstood me...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (They probably didn't... They could tell right away what a gullible girl you are.)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (Smiles)

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: I-Is that funny?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: No, my friend here may be a little shy around strangers, but she seems to be worried about you.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: *Cough*...

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Huh? W-Why, thanks! It's okay. I'm just lost, and since I saw a lighthouse here, I thought I'd come rest in here a little...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: I-I was lost, yes...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: No, that isn't what I was asking. You said this used to be a lighthouse?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Oh, yes. You can find lighthouses everywhere in Iberia. Have you never seen one before?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Hm... Perhaps they're only seen along the coastline. I've been away for about half a year now, and the towns farther from the coast don't have lighthouses.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Did you grow up by the sea?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Yes, and not far away from here. It's a small town, so you probably haven't heard of it.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: How is it doing...?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Okay... I guess?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: There aren't that many people, so we all got along well. My teacher said we were lucky. The sea's disasters spared our home.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Phew... That's great.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Well... except our lighthouse. Ever since that day, our lighthouse has never lit up again.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Since that day?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Right, that one day several decades ago. The day when disaster struck.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: In that one brief moment, the entire Iberian coastline was shrouded in darkness.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Ever since... it's never lit up again.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Aria, you seem rather familiar with lighthouses.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Why, that's because I grew up in one.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: In a lighthouse like this...?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Please don't get the wrong idea. My town's lighthouse is in much better condition. There wasn't a lot of damage, it just won't light up anymore.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: The mechanical parts, the central control system, the power circuits, the automation core, the outside wall Hologram emitter, and the wireless communications were all fine.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: My teacher would take me around the lighthouse every day to inspect and maintain everything, according to the manual. We even repaired the outside walls regularly.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Why, I can confidently say that, aside from the aging materials, our lighthouse is in just as great a condition as it was decades ago.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: That's amazing...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Your eyes light up when you're talking about your lighthouse... Just like when I talk to anyone else about Franker.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Do you and your teacher manage lighthouses?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry if I forgot to mention. Yes, my teacher is a glorious lighthouse keeper.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: As for me... I'm afraid I'm not there yet... A lighthouse only needs one official keeper, and I, uh, I'm just an apprentice...

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: And it's been so long since I left... so I guess I'm not even an apprentice anymore. *Sigh*...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You left long ago, but you still remember all the steps like the back of your hand.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: That's because I recite them before bed every night!

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You really love your job, Aria.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: I want to see the scenery my teacher described to me. It was something her teacher had described to her too.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Under the night sky, a multitude of intersecting courses in the sea lit up by the lighthouse.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: All the grand drilling rigs and sea forts glimmering in the dark as ships large and small come and go in their surroundings... It was far more bustling than any city on land and far more radiant than even when the sun burned its brightest...

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: If you got close enough, you could even see the underwater cities that the Iberian Ægirs built along the continental shelf.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: All of this was possible thanks to the thousands of lighthouses that stood on the Iberian coastline.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Now, disaster struck our energy system. None of the lighthouses can ever light up again as they once did.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Yet my teacher and I stayed to tend to the lighthouse.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Every night, my teacher would try to light it. The signal lamp doesn't work, so we made a new light source.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Our light source may not be able to stand in for a real lighthouse and illuminate the whole sea around us, only a small corner.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: And ships may long have stopped sailing the sea—

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: But we are still here.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: And you'll be there to watch the lighthouse even if the coast will remain forever silent?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Yes, we will.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: This is the top of the lighthouse.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: I inspected it a couple days ago. The lighthouse is in a really bad shape... There was hardly anything left of it before.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: This is the only thing still here.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: What is it...?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: It's a kind of energy core that Iberian lighthouses use. The most advanced technology they use... and also the first to be destroyed.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Is it broken?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: The original technology was lost... Neither I nor my teacher could restore its design. Without the complete energy system, we don't have a way to use the core to its full potential.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Perhaps... Hm... If you don't mind, I would like to take this back to Rhodes Island and inspect it with Closure.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh... I'm not saying I have a good grasp of this... Iberian technologies from those days have some really special wiring... Just like this core. All I can tell is that it's not based around Originium technology.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It doesn't use Originium as its energy source?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Not quite. It most likely still uses Originium for its energy, but... the foundation of the technology is very different. I'm even thinking that perhaps Originium energy isn't the best power source for this device.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: W-What's the matter? Is what I am talking about too boring...?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Can you really light up the lighthouse again?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: I think it's worth a try. It may take a while.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: I... I think I want to come with you.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Does that Rhodes Island you two are talking about need people like me? I don't know much... but... I'll work as hard as I can.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: First, you need a resume.

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: What's a resume? I...

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Mm... Weird... Why, I'm feeling kind of dizzy...

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: She passed out. What's the matter?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (Shrugs)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Oh... did she get poisoned?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Here I was thinking that Phidia is immune to my toxins, like you are.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Though it looks like it just took longer for it to affect her.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: (How should I say this? Perhaps her body isn't special in anyway. She's just... a little slow?)

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: (Let's not analyze this right now. D-Do you have an antidote? You're out on a mission with me alone, so you got to have one, right...?)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Relax. The paralysis is temporary.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Let's head outside. She should come around after she gets a little breeze.

steps.name: Glaucus
steps.text: Disable EMP field.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Finally! How are you, ladies? Have you run into any trouble?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Only a brief interlude...

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: *Cough*...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Oh, you're finally awake?

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: Sorry, it seems like I fell asleep...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: You came back around sooner than I expected.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: No need to worry. Our investigation was a success.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So why can I hear a third person? Sounds like a young lady with whom I've not had the pleasure...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: We met her at the mission location. Her name is Aria, and she gave us some valuable information. She'll be coming with us to Rhodes Island to hand PR her resume.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ah, well, let me welcome you in advance!

steps.name: Aria
steps.text: H-Hello...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Right, in conclusion, this was a lighthouse.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hm? A lighthouse? Did I hear that right? Our informant said it was 'really complicated by the looks.'

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: (I thought it was some important facility...)

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It was built before that disaster in Iberia.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I get it now...

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: The inner structure is still pretty intact, though the related technologies suffered heavy damage. We don't know for sure how much we can retrieve from here.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: And let the engineering team following this up know—

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: This place has the potential to become a new Rhodes Island office.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: *Sigh*... If this actually ends up becoming a new office, I will probably have to run back and forth all the time, won't I?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: And it's so close to that place too...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Well, I guess we don't exactly have much choice. We aren't the only ones that need this, either. The informant said there's been some refugees who escaped the destroyed towns to the south. They have a tough journey ahead, and they'll need someone to look out for them.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Right. Perhaps this lighthouse... will end up being fairly useful.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: We can provide medical services for the Infected in the area and help those in need, and we can... watch the tides that draw towards the land closer and closer day after day.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: It may not shine upon the area anymore... but it can still watch over this coastline.
